Q: React Native alternative to HTMLVideoElement.captureStream() for streaming a local video file to mediasoup (WebRTC)? A:

The core issue is that react-native-webrtc is a wrapper around Google's libwebrtc, which is designed primarily for hardware-based capturers (Camera/Microphone). It lacks a "Virtual Capturer" for file buffers out of the box.

Here are the two most practical ways to solve this:

1. Server-Side Injection (Recommended)

Instead of pushing bytes from a mobile device (consuming massive upload bandwidth and battery), upload the file to your server and use FFmpeg to inject it into your mediasoup PlainTransport.

Workflow:

  1. Upload file to server.

  2. Create a PlainTransport on the mediasoup router.

  3. Run FFmpeg to stream the file via RTP:


ffmpeg -re -i local_file.mp4 \
  -map 0:v:0 -c:v libx264 -payload_type 101 -f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:VIDEO_PORT \
  -map 0:a:0 -c:a opus -payload_type 102 -f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:AUDIO_PORT

2. Client-Side: FFmpeg-Kit to RTP

If the file must be processed on the device, you can use ffmpeg-kit-react-native to read the file and stream it to a local/remote RTP port that mediasoup listens to.

  • Pros: Keeps processing on the client.

  • Cons: Extremely CPU intensive for mobile devices; may cause frame drops.

A Note on Simplifying Your Infrastructure

Building custom WebRTC pipelines for React Native—especially when dealing with file-to-stream conversions—requires significant boilerplate. If you are looking for a way to manage these complexities without building the entire backend from scratch, WebLiveHub offers a Universal Server SDK (PHP) that handles the heavy lifting of WebRTC ingestion and distribution.

It generates optimized JavaScript for the frontend and simplifies the backend logic, allowing you to focus on the application experience rather than the underlying RTP/SDP handshaking. Check the Integration Guide for more technical details.

Q: Android Zebra / WebView drops session cookie after AJAX login over intranet HTTP, works on desktop browsers (SameSite/Secure?) A:

Android Zebra / WebView drops session cookie after AJAX login over intranet HTTP, works on desktop browsers (SameSite/Secure?)

Asked today

Modified today

Viewed 37 times

Part of PHP and Mobile Development Collectives

1

I’m running a web app on an intranet IP over plain HTTP and seeing inconsistent login behavior on a Zebra PDA using an Android embedded browser or WebView. Desktop browsers work reliably.

Login is handled via AJAX. The server returns success and sets a session cookie, then the client redirects to /dashboard.

$.ajax({

url: "/login/login",

type: "POST",

data: $("#quickForm").serialize(),

dataType: "json",

success: function (data) {

if (data.status) window.location.href = "/dashboard";

}

});

The login response includes a Set-Cookie header. On desktop browsers the cookie is always persisted and the redirect works. On the Zebra device the redirect sometimes succeeds but the session is missing on /dashboard, as if the cookie was never stored. Retrying the same login often works without changes, which makes this feel timing- or platform-dependent rather than a logic bug.

The app is accessed using an intranet IP like:

http://10.246.142.20/LPM/

The session cookie is configured with attributes similar to:

Set-Cookie: ci_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=None

or sometimes:

Set-Cookie: ci_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

There are no JavaScript errors on the device.

Are there known cases where Android embedded browsers or WebView ignore or delay Set-Cookie headers from AJAX responses on non-HTTPS origins due to SameSite or Secure rules, and what is the correct way to configure session cookies to make AJAX login reliable on both desktop browsers and Android embedded browsers?

Q: How do I solve Shopify's Oauth matching hosts error? A:

I solved it.

In 2026 the Shopify ecosystem has split app development into two categories: Custom Apps for private integrations that only are connected to one store, and Public Apps which are designed to be installed on multiple stores and are public-facing. Custom App config is accessed in the Admin Dashboard while Public App config is in the Dev Dashboard.

I had installed each type of app without realizing they were different. In my backend code I was using my API credentials for a Custom App when I needed to connect to my Public App. Once I switched the credentials everything worked properly.

NOTE: I had already created a Version of the Public App with the correct app url and api redirect listed.

Q: In writing a scanner in C: is my approach right and optimal? Should I continue writing it in C? Any references or guidelines? A:

If you want to parse something, a language with good string support is better, so while C++ isn't my favourite language, it would be better in this case than C.

That said, is there a reason for only those two? Python would be far easier. Java, C#, and many others have good string handling and regular expression support as well.

Q: How to Use Pydantic Model as Query Parameter in Litestar GET Route A:

I've encountered the same problem, and solved it like this:

import uvicorn
from litestar.openapi import OpenAPIConfig
from litestar.openapi.plugins import SwaggerRenderPlugin
from litestar.openapi.spec import Server
from pydantic import BaseModel
from litestar import Litestar, get, Controller


class Input(BaseModel):
    foo: str
    bar: str


class RootController(Controller):
    path = "/"

    @get()
    def input(
        self,
        query: Input
    ) -> str:
        return query.foo + query.bar


app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[RootController],
    openapi_config=OpenAPIConfig(
        title="API V1 LITESTAR",
        version="0.0.1",
        path="/docs",
        servers=[
            Server(url="/", description="API V1 LITESTAR"),
        ],
        render_plugins=[SwaggerRenderPlugin(path="/")],
    ),
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

If make a request with:

curl -X 'GET' \
'http://localhost:8000?foo=foo_value&bar=bar_value'

The response:

foo_valuebar_value%

But only problem is, I can not generate OpenAPI documentation for these params, eather using Litestar documentation. I've tried each method but in OpenAPI schema no any documented query param.

The key solution here is keyword 'query' in method's param. Litestar has reserved some keywords how I know, is lean on param's name for recognision, what it will be. So, if I'll replace the kwarg query into a data and the get method into post - the Input will be took from the body and OpenAPI documentation for it will be generated. The code example:

import uvicorn
from litestar.openapi import OpenAPIConfig
from litestar.openapi.plugins import SwaggerRenderPlugin
from litestar.openapi.spec import Server
from pydantic import BaseModel
from litestar import Litestar, Controller, post


class Input(BaseModel):
    foo: str
    bar: str


class RootController(Controller):
    path = "/"

    @post()
    def input(
        self,
        data: Input
    ) -> str:
        return data.foo + data.bar


app = Litestar(
    route_handlers=[RootController],
    openapi_config=OpenAPIConfig(
        title="API V1 LITESTAR",
        version="0.0.1",
        path="/docs",
        servers=[
            Server(url="/", description="API V1 LITESTAR"),
        ],
        render_plugins=[SwaggerRenderPlugin(path="/")],
    ),
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)

Request:

curl -X 'POST' \
'http://localhost:8000' \
-d '{"foo":"foo_value","bar":"bar_value"}'

Response:

foo_valuebar_value%
